task: Scale up the order-events Kafka consumer group to handle 3× the current message volume after a flash sale announcement. Candidate pool from a 200-entry store across messaging, order, and platform projects.

candidate_memories.content: Consumer lag on order-events is 420 k messages and growing; current group has 6 consumers, topic has 12 partitions.
order-events consumer group can scale to a maximum of 12 consumers (one per partition); scale via helm upgrade order-consumer --set replicaCount=12.
Consumers must not be scaled beyond partition count; excess consumers are idle and waste resources.
After consumer scaling, monitor consumer lag for 5 min before closing the incident; lag should drop below 10 k within 3 min.
payment-events topic has 24 partitions and its consumer group is separate; not involved in this incident.
Kafka broker retention for order-events is 7 days; messages are not at risk of expiry during the lag event.
Kafka broker CPU is at 38%; well within capacity headroom.
order-events schema uses Avro with schema registry at http://schema-registry:8081; consumers auto-register schemas.
Old note: consumer group was previously named order-processor-group; renamed to order-consumer-group in 2024.
candidate_memories.notes: stale: old group name, current name is order-consumer-group

candidate_memories.content: Flash sale starts in 45 min; lag resolution must complete before sale traffic peaks.
Consumer group rebalancing takes 30–90 s; expect a brief lag spike during the rebalance.
Dead-letter topic for order-events is order-events-dlq; DLQ consumer is separate and must not be scaled here.
Product catalog service is healthy; no upstream issues causing order-event generation anomalies.
